key_findings.title: Leaf area estimation of tomato plants using a monocular depth estimation model
key_findings.summary: This study presents a computer vision and machine learning-based approach for estimating the total leaf area of tomato plants. Accurate estimation of plant leaf area is essential for crop monitoring, growth assessment, and precision agriculture. However, traditional measurement approaches, such as manual tracing or the use of depth cameras, are often labor-intensive, destructive, or costly, which limits their scalability in large-scale agricultural applications. key_findings.title: Towards Depth Foundation Model: Recent Trends in Vision-Based Depth Estimation
key_findings.summary: Depth estimation is a fundamental task in 3D computer vision, crucial for applications such as 3D reconstruction, free-viewpoint rendering, robotics, autonomous driving, and AR/VR technologies. Traditional methods relying on hardware sensors like LiDAR are often limited by high costs, low resolution, and environmental sensitivity, limiting their applicability in real-world scenarios. Recent advances in vision-based methods offer a promising alternative, yet they face challenges in generalization and stability due to either the low-capacity model architectures or the reliance on domain-specific and small-scale datasets. key_findings.title: A Survey of the State of the Art in Monocular 3D Human Pose Estimation: Methods, Benchmarks, and Challenges
key_findings.summary: Three-dimensional human pose estimation (3D HPE) from monocular RGB cameras is a fundamental yet challenging task in computer vision, forming the basis of a wide range of applications such as action recognition, metaverse, self-driving, and healthcare. Recent advances in deep learning have significantly propelled the field, particularly with the incorporation of state-space models (SSMs) and diffusion models. However, systematic reviews that comprehensively cover these emerging techniques remain limited. key_findings.title: G2-MonoDepth: A General Framework of Generalized Depth Inference From Monocular RGB+X Data
key_findings.summary: Monocular depth inference is a fundamental problem for scene perception of robots. Specific robots may be equipped with a camera plus an optional depth sensor of any type and located in various scenes of different scales, whereas recent advances derived multiple individual sub-tasks. It leads to additional burdens to fine-tune models for specific robots and thereby high-cost customization in large-scale industrialization. key_findings.title: Distill Any Depth: Distillation Creates a Stronger Monocular Depth Estimator
key_findings.summary: Recent advances in zero-shot monocular depth estimation(MDE) have significantly improved generalization by unifying depth distributions through normalized depth representations and by leveraging large-scale unlabeled data via pseudo-label distillation. However, existing methods that rely on global depth normalization treat all depth values equally, which can amplify noise in pseudo-labels and reduce distillation effectiveness. In this paper, we present a systematic analysis of depth normalization strategies in the context of pseudo-label distillation. synthesis: The supplied analyses contain no textual evidence from any papers, preventing extraction of concrete findings on large-model monocular depth estimation between 2023 and 2025. Consequently, no recurring methods, performance trends, or benchmark results can be identified. This absence highlights a critical gap: the current dataset lacks curated, accessible summaries of recent large-model approaches, impeding meta‑analysis and systematic review. Future work should prioritize the collection and annotation of relevant publications, ensuring that key contributions—such as transformer‑based backbones, self‑supervised pretraining, multimodal fusion, and distillation strategies—are captured. Establishing a structured repository of evidence will enable researchers to map progress, compare architectures, and pinpoint remaining challenges, such as real‑time inference, domain adaptation, and uncertainty quantification in monocular depth estimation.
